name: application-comment-thread
title: Comment Thread
description: Nested reply chain with avatars, timestamps, a like count, reply affordance, and a composer footer.
useWhen: Showing a discussion with parent comments and nested replies, such as on a pull request, issue, or post.
Users need to both read a conversation and add to it in the same surface, via the composer footer.
Replies have a clear one-level parent/child relationship you want to convey with indentation.
avoidWhen: The conversation is a flat, real-time message exchange between two or more people — use `chat-bubbles` instead.
You don't need threading — a flat list of comments without replies is simpler without the nested `<ol>` and indent rail.
Replies can nest more than one level deep — this pattern's single indent rail does not represent deeper nesting; consider a recursive tree pattern instead.
responsiveBehavior: Stacks in a single column at all widths; the reply indent rail keeps a fixed pixel offset so deeply nested threads should be avoided on narrow viewports.
accessibility: Comments and replies are list items (<ol>/<li>) so assistive tech announces thread structure and position.
The composer textarea has an associated (visually hidden) label rather than relying on placeholder text alone.
The submit button is disabled when the draft is empty, communicated via the disabled attribute rather than only visual dimming.
Avatar images are decorative (empty alt) since the author name is present as adjacent text.

variants.title: Comment Thread
variants.description: A top-level comment with one nested reply and a comment composer.
accessibility: Reply threading is conveyed structurally via nested <ol> elements, not just visual indentation.

variants.title: Comment Thread (Dark)
variants.description: Comment thread adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Text and border colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
